utility.notes: Duke Energy (operating in Durham as Duke Energy Progress) serves most net-metering customers in North Carolina per the state's own Public Staff page — see the identical utility-identity notes on the Raleigh record (nc-wake-raleigh-duke).

value.name: Duke Energy Progress
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Durham's residential solar customers this session; Duke Energy Progress is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Durham operates a consolidated City-County Building & Safety Department, which serves as the single permitting authority for both the City of Durham and unincorporated Durham County.

permit_authority.notes: North Carolina uses a statewide North Carolina State Building Code (administered with the NC Office of State Fire Marshal), but permit issuance and enforcement is delegated locally. Durham's City-County Building & Safety Department is a genuinely consolidated jurisdiction serving both the City of Durham and Durham County under one department — distinct from most other North Carolina localities researched this session, which have separate city and county building departments.

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical statewide North Carolina net-metering framework notes on the Raleigh record (nc-wake-raleigh-duke) — Duke Energy customers fall under Rider RSC or the capacity-limited Rider NMB as of the 2023-10-01 policy transition; residential systems are capped at 20kW AC.

value.name: Building Permit application (required for PV arrays on one- and two-family dwellings, depending on roof condition/structural integrity)

Construction drawings — one copy of plans showing PV array configuration, wiring system, overcurrent protection, inverter, disconnects, required signs, AC connection to building, and attachment/footing detail (roof- or ground-mounted), engineer-stamped
Specification sheets and installation manuals for all manufactured components (PV modules, inverters, combiner box, disconnects, mounting system)

required_documents.notes: Per the Department's own 'Solar Photovoltaic (PV) System Permitting Requirements' document (Doc. 26268, Rev. 08-11-2025). One- and two-family installations must comply with the 2018 North Carolina Residential Code. Applications and documentation are submitted through the City's online Dplans portal.

value: Inspections are scheduled through the Land Development Office webpage
Inspections are typically completed within 24 hours of an inspection request

timeline_days.notes: The Department's own document states only that it makes 'best efforts' to provide timely review, without a specific day-count, and lists factors that can prolong turnaround (incomplete applications, unlicensed contractors, unlisted equipment). Permits expire 6 months after issuance if no inspection has been conducted.

other_conditions: Ground-mounted panels for single/two-family homes outside historic districts must be at least 6 feet from property lines; no screening is required for ground- or roof-mounted systems

Properties in historic districts require a Minor Certificate of Appropriateness (COA) for ground-mounted systems if street visibility is minimized (otherwise a Major COA), and for roof-mounted systems that are rear-facing and do not damage historic roofing materials
Permits expire 6 months after issuance if no inspection has been conducted; once work begins, noticeable progress must continue until completion

permit_fees.notes: The Department's own document points to a separate 'Building Permit Fee Schedule G' and 'Electrical Permit Fee Schedule G' rather than stating a specific dollar figure directly — left null rather than estimated.

rebates.notes: No statewide North Carolina or Durham-specific solar rebate/tax-credit program was independently confirmed this session — left null rather than guessed.
